name: Hassan ibn Thabit
bio: Abu al-Walid Hassan ibn Thabit, of the Khazraj of Medina, was a Companion and the Prophet's poet. He belonged to the generation that knew both the pagan age and Islam, and is said to have lived sixty years in each. Before Islam he was known for his praise of the Ghassanid princes and the kings of al-Hira; afterwards he became the Prophet's poet and a fierce satirist of his enemies. Abu Ubayda said he surpassed other poets in three ways: he was the poet of the Ansar before Islam, of the Prophet during his mission, and of the Yemenis in Islam. He went blind near the end of his life and died in Medina in 54 AH (674 CE).
